title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Lehigh spaces where students can study individually, collaborate, meet, or work near campus resources.

cards.title: Match the Room to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Five floors of individual and collaborative study options
cards.notes: Use the quiet north side for solo work or the conversation-friendly south side when your group needs movable furniture and whiteboards.
cards.short_summary: A flexible library where students can choose between quiet concentration and active collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries says Fairchild-Martindale provides five floors of collaborative spaces, classrooms, study nooks, meeting rooms, and open study areas.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Check the current Libraries hours page before visiting; a Lehigh ID is required for library entry after 9 p.m.

cards.title: Read Beneath the Rotunda
cards.subtitle: Historic architecture with quiet nooks and group rooms
cards.notes: Choose the first-floor Reading Room for open seating, a stack-side nook for quieter work, or a study room when conversation is necessary.
cards.short_summary: The historic library combines a grand shared reading room with smaller spaces among the collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries documents Linderman's rotunda, quiet stack-side nooks, individual and group study rooms, and first-floor Reading Room.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Check current library hours before visiting; public research access is available, but a Lehigh ID is required after 9 p.m.

cards.title: Bring the Work That Needs a Screen
cards.subtitle: Flexible seating, computers, displays, and portable whiteboards
cards.notes: Set up here when a project benefits from a Windows workstation, a laptop-ready wall display, movable whiteboard, or charging-equipped seat.
cards.short_summary: A technology-oriented work area suited to both individual tasks and screen-based collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries describes first-level open study space with flexible seating, mobile chargers, portable whiteboards, Windows computers, and laptop-ready displays.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: The Computing Center remains open 24/7; current library guidance requires Lehigh ID tap entry after 6 p.m. weekdays and all day weekends.

cards.title: Shift Your Work to Mountaintop
cards.subtitle: Open and semi-private seating beside creative disciplines
cards.notes: Use the open areas for an informal working session or seek a semi-private spot when you need fewer distractions between Mountaintop commitments.
cards.short_summary: A cross-disciplinary Mountaintop building with two levels of less-obvious study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries says Mountaintop Building C houses Art, Architecture and Design and Computer Science and offers open and semi-private study spaces on both levels.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Located at 113 Research Drive; confirm current building access before making a dedicated trip to Mountaintop Campus.

cards.title: Use the Gaps Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Classrooms, a lobby, and upper-level study carrels
cards.notes: Check whether a first-floor classroom is between sessions; otherwise move upstairs to the second-floor lobby or a quieter upper-level carrel.
cards.short_summary: An academic building with several practical ways to turn schedule gaps into working time.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries says students may use Maginnes Hall's first-floor classrooms when classes are not in session, plus its lobby and upper-level study carrels.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Classroom use is limited to times when classes are not in session; verify posted access and avoid disrupting scheduled activity.

cards.title: Choose Sunlight or a Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Galleria seating upstairs from lower-level computing
cards.notes: Take reading or laptop work to the first-floor galleria; head to the lower-level computer labs when the assignment requires campus equipment.
cards.short_summary: One building offers a brighter informal work area and more task-focused computer facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries identifies the first-floor galleria and lower-level computer labs in Rauch Business Center as student work locations.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Located at 621 Taylor Street; building and lab access may follow academic schedules, so check current campus information.

cards.title: Work Along the Glass Atrium
cards.subtitle: Small-group seating spread through a six-floor science building
cards.notes: Try the first-floor open areas for easy access, then move to upper-level seating or the second-floor glass atrium when you need a change of setting.
cards.short_summary: A science building where open seating is distributed beyond the most visible ground-floor areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries says STEPS has first-floor open spaces, individual and small-group seating across six floors, and a glass atrium facing Packer Avenue.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Located at 1 West Packer Avenue; confirm current academic-building access and yield seating needed for scheduled activities.

cards.title: Meet Where Making Is Visible
cards.subtitle: An active setting near computing, design, and fabrication labs
cards.notes: Bring collaborative or creative work that benefits from a conversation-friendly setting and the energy of nearby design and fabrication activity.
cards.short_summary: A creative facility whose active atmosphere fits discussion-heavy and design-oriented work.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries describes Wilbur Powerhouse as a 17,000-square-foot creative facility with computing, additive, creativity, and design labs and conversation-friendly spaces.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: This is an active academic facility; confirm current access and follow any lab-specific authorization or safety requirements.

cards.title: Follow the Building Upward
cards.subtitle: Event space below, greenhouse and terrace seating above
cards.notes: Check Roemmele Global Plaza when no event is scheduled, or continue upstairs to the glass-enclosed Torcivia Greenhouse and Maida Family Terrace.
cards.short_summary: Williams Hall rewards exploring beyond its entrance with several distinct working environments.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries says students may use Roemmele Global Plaza when free and identifies Torcivia Greenhouse and Maida Family Terrace as spaces for group or individual study.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: Roemmele Global Plaza is available only when not occupied by a university event; confirm current building and terrace access.

cards.title: Watch for Study Night at the Museum
cards.subtitle: A finals-period pop-up workspace among gallery exhibitions
cards.notes: Check LUAG's finals programming before going; when Study Night is scheduled, bring quiet work and use gallery walks as short screen breaks.
cards.short_summary: A documented finals event temporarily turns an art gallery into a student study setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Lehigh Libraries documents Study Night at the Museum in the LUAG Lower Gallery as a quiet pop-up study space offered during the first week of final exams.
cards.source_title: Places and Spaces: Top 10 great study spots on campus
cards.access_notes: This study use is event-dependent, not daily access; verify the current LUAG calendar and Zoellner entry conditions before visiting.
